title: San Francisco physicians who hold a stake in a drug or device maker
question: Which San Francisco physicians, or their close family, hold an ownership or investment interest in a company that makes drugs or devices, what else has the company paid them, and do the files show them using its products?
finding: 41 San Francisco physicians hold or held interests in 35 manufacturers in the federal disclosure files for 2019 to 2025; the 22 interests reported for 2025 are valued at $14.6 million. The largest at its latest report is Tony Chou's interest in Route 92 Medical, Inc. ($4.9 million, 2025). 5 physicians hold interests in one company, Route 92 Medical, Inc. 16 of the holders were also paid by the same company ($10.2 million in all), the most being Daniel Schwartz from RxSight Inc ($8.0 million, mostly "compensation for services other than consulting, including serving as faculty or as a speaker at a venue other than a continuing education program"). The Medicare drug file shows 0 of them prescribing a product the company names. These records are the manufacturers' own public disclosures.
how: Every ownership or investment record with a San Francisco address in the federal Open Payments files, one row per physician and company, showing the latest year reported. Beside each: general payments from the same company to the same provider number in the same years, with the largest category as the company described it; research payments from that company on studies where the physician is a principal investigator; and whether any product the company names in its payment records appears, under the same brand name, among the drugs that physician prescribed in the Medicare drug file for San Francisco.
limits: Ownership interests and payments from manufacturers are disclosed by the companies themselves; a row is a disclosure, not an accusation. Some holders work for the company (one record's terms say so), and some of the payments are themselves labelled by the company as "current or prospective ownership or investment interest". Of the 10 companies here whose payment records name a product, 9 name a device or medical supply. No public file on disk records which brand of device a surgeon implants or orders, so the link the question asks about cannot be tested for them; the drug-file check can only catch a prescribed brand-name drug. Values are as the company reported them and can be stale or zero. The file lists only what manufacturers reported; anything a physician owns that was not reported this way is not here.
